put.description: Creates a new HorizonDB cluster or replaces an existing cluster. PointInTimeRestore creates the new Cluster resource and hydrates its service-owned database storage from an available source backup. It does not clone source pools, Pool-scoped endpoints, firewall rules, parameter-group associations, or other child resources. The new Cluster receives its service-generated Cluster-scoped Endpoint named cluster. PostgreSQL version is inherited from backup metadata; all other new-cluster configuration comes from the request or service defaults. Until cross-region point-in-time restore is supported, the target cluster location must match the source cluster location; a cross-region request is rejected synchronously with 400 CrossRegionPointInTimeRestoreNotSupported and does not create or modify a resource.

patch.description: Updates the service-created PostgreSQL username-and-password authentication method. The request is sparse and omitted properties preserve their current values. A state-only request enables or disables the authentication mechanism; disabling cannot include credentials and does not remove or modify existing database users or roles. Login-only, password-only, and combined credential updates require this method to already be Enabled unless this request also sets state to Enabled. PostgreSQL is the sole source of truth; the control plane stores no administrator identity or credentials. The service bootstraps an AzureSU-owned special group, only AzureSU can grant or revoke its membership, and at most one user role can be a member. Login-only or password-only updates require exactly one current member. A combined administratorLogin and administratorLoginPassword request creates and adds a new user when no member exists, resets the password when the member name matches, or renames the member and resets its password when names differ. A requested name that already exists outside the special group is rejected to prevent privilege elevation. Both authentication methods may be Disabled.

put.description: Creates a new HorizonDB pool or updates an existing pool, including its desired node allocation, compute model, or associated parameter group. A pool name can be the same as its parent cluster name. Creating a pool also creates exactly one service-managed Pool-scoped ReadOnly Endpoint representing that Pool and its network boundary. The Endpoint's associatedResourceId identifies the Pool, and the Endpoint cannot outlive or be deleted independently from it. When the first pool is created, the service automatically uses it to host the cluster's read-write node when an eligible node is available. This API version supports at most one pool per cluster; an attempt to create another pool is rejected with 409 Conflict. Every pool must be associated with a parameter group, so parameterGroup, parameterGroupResourceId, and applyMethod are required. applyMethod controls when dynamic parameter changes become effective; static parameter changes always require a customer-triggered restart or a restart during scheduled maintenance. For a Serverless compute model, the service validates that minVCores is less than or equal to maxVCores. A request that would leave the pool hosting the read-write node with an effective desiredNodeCount of 0 is rejected without changing the pool.

After the Pool is running, its Pool-scoped ReadOnly Endpoint routes only when at least one allocated node is not currently playing the read-write role. post.description: Switches this replica cluster with its immediate source while preserving the replication set and descendant relationships. The operation is valid only when the cluster has the Target role. Before starting, a virtual endpoint must exist whose writer targets the Cluster-scoped Endpoint named cluster in the immediate source Cluster and whose reader targets the Cluster-scoped Endpoint named cluster in this direct replica; otherwise the service rejects the request with 409 VirtualEndpointSwitchoverPreconditionFailed. On success, the service atomically swaps the replication topology, changes the invoked replica's Cluster-scoped Endpoint role to ReadWrite, changes the former source's Cluster-scoped Endpoint role to ReadOnly, and swaps the virtual endpoint writer and reader resource IDs and DNS CNAME destinations. If the topology, role, or endpoint retarget cannot commit, the service rolls back all changes and reports a failed operation.

VirtualEndpoint.description: Represents stable writer and reader DNS aliases for a HorizonDB replication topology. For regional resilience, customers should deploy the VirtualEndpoint in an Azure region that has a paired region and that is different from every Cluster region in the referenced replication set. This is a recommendation only: the service does not validate or enforce it, and any otherwise supported location remains accepted. Separating the VirtualEndpoint control-plane resource from all replication-set Cluster regions can help it survive a regional outage affecting the root Cluster and remain available for promote or switchover recovery workflows, but does not guarantee availability.

readerEndpointResourceId.description: The Azure resource ID of the Cluster-scoped Endpoint that receives reader traffic. The target must be the Endpoint named cluster in the writer Cluster or one of its direct level-1 replica Clusters; indirect descendants are not valid targets. The target role is topology-derived: the writer Cluster's Endpoint is ReadWrite when that Cluster is the current root, while a direct replica Cluster's Endpoint is ReadOnly because its replication.roles contains Target.
